originalTitle: Russian anti-war politician says he has fled the country
summary: Boris Nadezhdin, who was recently designated as a foreign agent, posted a video in front of the Eiffel Tower.
content:
Boris Nadezhdin came to prominence two years ago when he tried to stand for the presidency on an anti-war platform

An anti-war politician who tried to challenge Vladimir Putin at the last Russian presidential election says he has fled the country after Moscow declared him a "foreign agent" last month.

Boris Nadezhdin posted a video standing in front of the Eiffel Tower in Paris.

He said: "Hi everyone. I have some good news. I'm alive and free. Unfortunately, I'm not in Russia at the moment."

Nadezhdin, 63, came to prominence two years ago when he tried to stand for the presidency on an anti-war platform, but was barred because electoral authorities ruled signatures he had submitted were flawed.

He was designated a "foreign agent" by the justice ministry last month after saying he would run as a candidate in September's Duma (parliamentary) elections.

Nadezhdin was accused of spreading false information about the Russian government and calling on people to take part in unauthorised rallies.

The label would have prevented him from taking part in the elections.

He was charged with "displaying extremist symbols" – a reference to an image of the late opposition leader Alexei Navalny, which appeared for 10 seconds in a video reposted by Nadezhdin's social media accounts in November 2023. He called the charge ridiculous.

Last week, he told BBC Russian from an undisclosed location that his prospects were "vague" after he was forced to abandon his campaign to run for parliament.

"If you're a politician, you should participate in politics while you have the opportunity. How do you participate in politics? By participating in elections," he said.

Then on Monday he posted a video to Telegram filmed in Paris, saying: "Right now, I need to get my bearings and figure out what to do next. I'll write about my plans later."

Speaking in an online video from the Eiffel Tower in Paris, Nadezhdin said he needed to figure out what to do next

In early 2024, Nadezhdin attempted to run as a presidential candidate on an anti-war manifesto, calling for an end to the hostilities in Ukraine.

At the time, he told the BBC that he was supported by "dozens of millions of people" who did not want "Russia to be in this track of authoritarianism and militarism".

He also said that if he was elected president his first task would be to "stop the conflict with Ukraine, and then to restore normal relations between Russia and the Western community".

However, his criticism of Putin remained measured, leading some to speculate the Kremlin would allow him to run so as to give the election the illusion of being fair.

Nadezhdin was eventually prevented from standing by the Russian electoral commission weeks before the vote took place, on the grounds that more than 15% of the signatures he submitted with his candidate application were flawed.

He contested this but was ultimately unable to run, as were any other credible opposition figures.

On 18 March 2024, Putin claimed a landslide victory which ushered in a fifth term in office.

The next presidential election is scheduled for 2030, when Putin will be 78. A constitutional amendment passed in 2020 reset his term limits, allowing him to remain in power until 2036.

Earlier this year, when the Kremlin began restricting internet access for millions across the country and Russia's economic crisis deepened, Nadezhdin told the BBC that people were "beginning to understand that there is a direct connection between their everyday problems, like healthcare, food prices, problems with internet and the politics of Vladimir Putin."

The Kremlin now wields near-total control over the Russian political landscape, and it is unlikely that anybody would be allowed to challenge Putin's rule.

The opposition figures who could have offered Russian voters an alternative are either in jail, in exile or dead.
chineseTitle: 俄罗斯反战政客称他已逃离该国
chineseSummary: 最近被指定为外国特工的鲍里斯·纳杰日丁在埃菲尔铁塔前发布了一段视频。
chineseContent:
鲍里斯·纳杰日丁两年前因试图以反战纲领竞选总统而声名鹊起

一位试图在上次俄罗斯总统选举中挑战弗拉基米尔·普京的反战政治家表示，在莫斯科上个月宣布他为“外国代理人”后，他已逃离该国。

鲍里斯·纳杰日丁发布了一段站在巴黎埃菲尔铁塔前的视频。

他说：“大家好。我有一些好消息。我还活着并且自由。不幸的是，我现在不在俄罗斯。”

63 岁的纳杰日丁两年前声名鹊起，当时他试图以反战纲领竞选总统，但因选举当局裁定他提交的签名存在缺陷而被禁止。

上个月，他表示将作为候选人参加九月的杜马（议会）选举，之后被司法部认定为“外国代理人”。

纳杰日丁被指控散布有关俄罗斯政府的虚假信息并呼吁人们参加未经授权的集会。

这个标签会阻止他参加选举。

他被指控“展示极端主义符号”——指的是已故反对派领导人阿列克谢·纳瓦尔尼的图像，该图像在纳杰日丁的社交媒体账户于 2023 年 11 月转发的视频中出现了 10 秒。他称这一指控十分荒谬。

上周，他在一个秘密地点告诉英国广播公司俄语频道，在被迫放弃竞选议会议员后，他的前景“模糊”。

“如果你是一名政治家，你应该在有机会的时候参与政治。你如何参与政治？通过参加选举，”他说。

然后周一，他向 Telegram 发布了一段在巴黎拍摄的视频，说道：“现在，我需要弄清楚自己的方位并弄清楚下一步该做什么。我稍后会写下我的计划。”

纳杰日丁在巴黎埃菲尔铁塔的在线视频中表示，他需要弄清楚下一步该做什么

2024 年初，纳杰日丁试图以反战宣言竞选总统候选人，呼吁结束乌克兰的敌对行动。

当时，他告诉英国广播公司，他得到了“数十万人”的支持，他们不希望“俄罗斯走上威权主义和军国主义的轨道”。

他还表示，如果当选总统，他的首要任务将是“停止与乌克兰的冲突，然后恢复俄罗斯与西方社会的正常关系”。

然而，他对普京的批评仍然谨慎，导致一些人猜测克里姆林宫将允许他参选，以便给选举带来公平的假象。

纳杰日丁最终在投票前几周被禁止加入俄罗斯选举委员会，理由是他在候选人申请中提交的签名中有超过 15% 有缺陷。

他对此提出异议，但最终未能参选，其他可信的反对派人物也是如此。

2024 年 3 月 18 日，普京获得压倒性胜利，开启第五个任期。

下一次总统选举定于 2030 年举行，届时普京将年满 78 岁。2020 年通过的宪法修正案重新设定了他的任期限制，允许他继续执政至 2036 年。

今年早些时候，当克里姆林宫开始限制全国数百万人的互联网接入以及俄罗斯经济危机加剧时，纳杰日丁告诉英国广播公司，人们“开始明白，他们的日常问题，如医疗保健、食品价格、互联网问题和弗拉基米尔·普京的政治之间存在直接联系。”

克里姆林宫现在几乎完全控制了俄罗斯的政治格局，不太可能允许任何人挑战普京的统治。

本来可以为俄罗斯选民提供另一种选择的反对派人物要么入狱，要么流亡，要么死亡。
